text:
laura: quick sync — sketching a PRD fragment for Dedicated capacity: need a decision on commit policy + sizing + canary / fallback playbook. customers pushing for 99.9% uptime SLA and stable p95 latency. thoughts?

jake: tagging numbers — do we mean p95 <= 150ms for small seqs or for 512 tokens?

laura: p95 target should be for typical payloads (avg seq 128). we'll call out longer seqs as a separate tier.

priya: agree. also need an autoscale constraint: scale-out within 30s for steady growth, but prevent oscillation on bursty traffic.

emily: from ops POV we want explicit warm-pool behavior: reserve X% of GPUs as warm for canaries. otherwise cold starts kill p95.

rob: customers asking about reserved commit flexibility — can they burst above commit for brief windows? pricing doc suggests burst credits but need clear limits in PRD.

laura: propose: baseline commit + burstable capacity with throttling and fallback. acceptance criteria should include cost delta for bursts < 1% month.

jake: suggested sizing heuristic in PRD draft: start with worst-case throughput targets per model variant: 
```
- small: 8000 tokens/s per V100-equivalent
- medium: 5000 tokens/s per A100-equivalent
- large: 2500 tokens/s per quantized A100
```
Those numbers are rough — need perf team validation.

priya: also include KV cache warmup story: during canary we pre-populate with typical prefixes to avoid cold-KV penalties.

laura: acceptance criteria (rough):
- release on Dedicated passes performance gate: p95 <= 150ms on avg seq=128, sustained for 30m under target load
- failover behaviour validated: when reserved pool exhausted, requests routed to burst pool or fallback model (with documented quality degradation)
- autoscale stability: no more than 2 scale actions/min per pool under sustained variance
- cost delta for typical tenant limited to +5% vs non-dedicated baseline

emily: add monitoring/alerts: token-level cost, p95 per-route, queued requests > 5s, warm-pool utilization < 30% or > 90%.

jake: edge cases we must enumerate:
- sudden hot-sharding: single tenant spikes and starves multi-tenant reserved pools
- model-specific cold start for large context windows
- quantization mismatch: fallback to unquantized model when requests need model ops not supported by quantized kernels
- region failover when network cross-region latency spikes

priya: for autoscale policy sample in PRD: use combined metric of queued_requests + avg_token_latency. scale-up when queued_requests>20 OR avg_token_latency>120ms for 3 consecutive 10s windows. scale-down with hysteresis: only after 10m below thresholds.

laura: include canary rollout steps:
1) 5% of traffic to new Dedicated pool, monitor p95/p99, error rate, cost.
2) if regressions <= tolerated thresholds, increase to 25% after 1h.
3) 100% after 24h stability.
Fallback: automatic rollback to previous pool and notify ENG on critical regressions.

rob: add contract language for committed capacity: minimum 3-month commit to enable Dedicated pricing; 2x-3x multiplier for rapid cancellations during burst windows? legal should advise.

emily: we need a playbook excerpt for incident ops in PRD: immediate mitigation steps when p95 breached for >10m: divert traffic to hosted, enable reduced-batch low-latency mode, temporarily increase warm-pool size.

jake: small note: quantify "hosted fallback" latency delta in PRD — e.g., hosted variant adds +40-80ms typical, mention token cost differences.

priya: add a test matrix for load tests: baseline, burst, noisy-neighbor, region-outage. each test must include SLO pass/fail criteria.

laura: placebo checklist for PRD review: requirements, explicit acceptance criteria above, rollout plan, ops/playbook, contract wording, cost modelling, test matrix, edge cases documented.

jake: I can take the sizing + autoscale policy section and mock numbers based on our bench next week.

priya: I'll write the canary + warm-pool runbook and test scenarios.

emily: I'll draft the incident/playbook and monitoring alerts.

rob: i'll get with legal on commit/cancellation language and pricing burst credits.

laura: thanks — aim to have first draft PRD in two working days. tagging @jake @priya @emily @rob for action items. :thumbsup:
